parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime imposes universal-exposure measures at every entry: the January 2025 orders force binary birth-sex markers on passports and visas, the February 2025 cable directs officers to refuse any applicant whose documents 'cast reasonable doubt' on sex and to consider lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation, and travellers report passport confiscation, stranding, and detentions that prompted allied governments to issue advisories. Facility bans in many state/provinces, criminalised bathroom use in 4, and documented birth-sex custody harms (corrections bureau, immigration detention abuse) define the national layer. The division adds no adult facility or care ban and no sodomy law, but no state recourse, no hate-crime coverage, and a draft youth-care ban affecting travelling minors. Worst feature is tier-1 state-imposed universal exposure with thin remedy: materially worse than 0.55 anchors, above execution-tier 0.05-0.15, comparable to a harsh 0.40.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: passports/visas forced to birth-sex markers; officers instructed to refuse cases with document discrepancies and consider permanent fraud bars; X-marker processing ended; reported confiscations and stranded travellers; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties suit ongoing; existing X passports valid until expiry; FAQ guidance exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Document check feeds directly into refusal, fraud finding, or investigation at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Foreign nationals detained over visa issues; national corrections bureau mandates birth-sex policies incl. hormone removal; immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal can escalate into immigration custody with documented birth-sex placement and abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars congruent facility use in government-funded single-sex facilities; 9+9+3 state/provinces ban; 4 criminalise in certain circumstances with a documented arrest (19 Mar 2025, men's-ward holding); this division has no statewide adult ban; one school-district birth-sex policy.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division: no adult facility statute; 29+ state/provinces without bans.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National and state bans operate in parallel across the journey.

care_services.exposure: Medication continuity uncertain; national hostility to care (funding freezes, subpoenas, proposed under-18 insurance bar).
care_services.protection: Division: no statewide adult care ban; municipal ordinances in 4 cities (~46% population) cover accommodations.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor's care access unaffected in this division; minor's access threatened by draft regulation (not yet operative).

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing: 'gender ideology' removals, 'radically pro-transgender' groups counterterrorism-prioritised, teachers criminally targeted for facilitating minor transitions, gender described as mutilation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Employment discrimination prohibited nationally (2020 ruling); national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and severity of any police encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor: care criminalised by discipline threat via draft regulation (pending); sports exclusion; EO directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; 27 state/provinces ban youth care.
minors_guardians.protection: Draft not yet operative in this division; no statewide adult or youth care ban here yet.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian whose minor is known to transition faces investigation exposure via schools and boards.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-violence counts or homicide denominator for the division; bias-crime penalty enhancement absent state-wide; no recourse outside four municipalities.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; municipal ordinances survive repeal vote.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to bias incidents outside municipalities is unsourced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No visitor recourse against discrimination outside 4 municipalities; passport policy in flux; fraud-bar waiver limited; enforcement of municipal ordinances unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation unresolved but live; legal-aid FAQ; equality maps/guidance available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether any given measure is operative at travel time is uncertain, extending exposure across the national layer.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal-exposure logic: registration/databases force disclosure of trans status to officials. Here the exposure is at the border itself (refusal, stranding, lifetime fraud bar) with a documented entry ban category and detention reports — heavier than 0.45-D's typical harms.

Like 0.35-A, entry can be denied on discretionary gender-norm grounds with no effective remedy; unlike it, exclusion is not the sole documented outcome — fraud ineligibility, custody with documented abuse, and facility criminalisation add severity, so not as low as 0.35.

0.55-C's harms are administrative denial with partial remedies; here remedies against the operative national measures are thin or failing (refusals upheld, custody harms recurring), and universal border exposure is harsher. The division alone would sit near 0.55; the combined regime pulls below it.

Not comparable to 0.15-C: no morality sweeps, no capital charging pathway, no documented coerced-confession pattern against visitors; state institutions, while hostile, still operate litigation and partial protections. Clearly above 0.15-0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The dominant exposure is national and universal: every crossing requires binary birth-sex documents, officers are instructed to refuse discrepancy cases and may impose permanent fraud bars, and document checks cascade into refusal, detention, or custody placement by birth sex where documented abuse exists. Facility bans and criminalised restroom use are state-variable, with this division imposing no adult ban but offering no recourse, no hate-crime enhancement, and a pending youth-care restriction that raises risk for travelling families. Municipal protections cover ~46% of the population only. No execution or systematic imprisonment pathway for visitors is documented, ruling out the lowest bands, but the tier-1 universal exposure with thin working remedies places the jurisdiction in the high-risk band, around 0.40.
